claims.text: Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a diffusion-limited ordering transformation.
Slow cooling permits Al, and possibly Cr, atoms to rearrange into a chemically ordered B2-type structure.
Formation of the B2-type structure lowers the alloy's free energy.
Rapid quenching kinetically traps a metastable disordered BCC state.
Heating Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 to approximately 1200°C produces a homogeneous high-temperature BCC state.
Slow cooling from approximately 1200°C to 600°C provides sufficient atomic diffusion for ordering.
Rapid quenching from approximately 1200°C freezes the high-temperature BCC state.
The temperature interval from approximately 1200°C to 600°C is critical for ordering in this alloy.
Slow cooling causes formation of B2-type ordered domains through diffusion and sublattice rearrangement.
At lower temperatures, the disordered BCC phase is thermodynamically unstable even though quenching can preserve it kinetically.
Slow-cooled samples will exhibit B2 superlattice reflections in XRD.
Slow-cooled samples will contain ordered domains observable by TEM.
Rapidly quenched samples will retain a uniform BCC diffraction pattern without ordering features.
The rapidly quenched baseline represents a kinetically trapped disordered BCC state.
The proposed mechanism may cease to apply if significant compositional segregation occurs or if temperatures extend substantially beyond 600–1200°C.

contradictions.description: Significant compositional segregation is treated as a condition outside the hypothesis's stated applicability, but ordering attributable to segregation is also described as falsifying the hypothesis. An excluded boundary condition is not, without further specification, a decisive falsification.
